This is an application for anticipatory bail filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
2. Petitioners are accused Nos. 1 to 3 in Crime No.494/2023 of Payyannur Police Station, Kannur District, registered for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.

The crime is registered on the basis of a complaint filed by the wife of the 1st petitioner, alleging that she was treated cruelly demanding dowry.
3. The marriage between the 1st petitioner and the 2nd respondent was conducted on 11.01.2015 and three children are born out of the wedlock.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioners,
difference of opinion arose between the spouses when the 2nd respondent demanded that she should be permitted to reside in her paternal house.
It is submitted that the allegations are patently false and if the petitioners are arrested in connection with the offence, that will cause irreparable injury and hardship to them.
4. I heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.
5. Considering the nature of allegation, custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not required.

Hence, application is allowed subject to the following conditions.
i. The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks.

ii. The investigating officer shall interrogate the petitioners and in the event of their arrest, the petitioners shall be Abdul Basith vs State Of Kerala on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88813043/
2 released on bail on their executing bond for Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) each with two solvent sureties, each for the like amount, to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional court.

The petitioners shall co-operate with the investigation and appear before the investigating officer as and when required.
